prior_importants.description: When `git rebase --abort` fails, the empty catch swallows it, and the gate now goes on to merge and land the branch. Before this change the same path stopped with a fail.

No test covers the new guard that stops an interrupted rebase from turning into a merge. If you delete `rethrowIfKilled(error);` at L2410, the whole suite still passes, but an interrupted rebase then merges and lands.

findings.description: No test reaches the `rethrowIfKilled(error)` inside the abort's catch, which handles a rebase killed before it starts. Deleting that line passes the suite, and a Ctrl-C then becomes a fresh-base failure steered to the worker.
findings.body:
**No test covers the interrupt check that runs when a rebase is killed before it starts.**

In `gateAndMerge`, the abort's catch begins with `rethrowIfKilled(error)` ([merge-gate.service.ts L2405-L2410](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4cf82073617fa6a485842d1b603a0edec69d1a69/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2405-L2410)). It only matters when two things happen together:
- the rebase was killed by a signal;
- the abort then failed.

That is the common Ctrl-C case. git dies before it writes any rebase state, so `git rebase --abort` exits 128 with "no rebase in progress".

None of the [`it.each` rows](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/4cf82073617fa6a485842d1b603a0edec69d1a69/src/core/merge-gate-fresh-base.test.ts#L195-L209) reach that line:
- **`['the rebase', isRebase, true]`:** the real rebase stops on its conflict, and the real abort succeeds. The catch is never entered, and the rethrow comes from the check after the abort (L2426).
- **`['the abort of a conflicting rebase', isAbort, false]`:** the rebase's error has no signal, so only `rethrowIfKilled(abortError)` fires.
- **The L211 test:** it uses `signal: null`.

**Mutant.** Delete L2408. A killed rebase followed by a failed abort then reaches `rethrowIfKilled(abortError)`, which does nothing because the abort's error has no signal. The gate then:
- pushes "Auto-rebase onto main failed and so did its abort";
- calls `failed()`, which goes through `rejectOrBlock`;
- counts a rejection and steers the worker, while the operator is the one interrupting.

The suite stays green. The merge lock keeps node alive through SIGINT (`LOCK_SIGNALS`), so in production this window is reachable.

The comment above the `it.each` is also wrong for the abort row. With `runFirst: false`, that abort never runs, so "the abort succeeds" is false.

**Fix.** Add a row `['the rebase before it starts', isRebase, false]`. The rebase is skipped and thrown as SIGINT, then the real abort fails, and only L2408 rethrows. Also correct the comment.

findings.description: The rebase catch now treats any error that is not an interrupt as a conflict and falls back to a merge that can pass. That includes `runGit`'s `RewrittenGitDirError` refusal, so the session-compromised warning is lost where it used to fail fresh-base. Rethrow any error without a numeric git `status` after the abort.

The 30-vs-1 test counts only `--is-ancestor` processes, which `holdsMergeOfTarget` never spawns. A rewrite that ran one `rev-list` or `merge-base` per merge parent under the merge lock would still pass. Count the git calls whose argv includes `rev-list` or `merge-base` to pin the "one git process" promise.

The `pup merge` JSDoc still describes fresh-base as an auto-rebase, with a merge of the target only for a branch an open PR holds. It does not mention decision 190's merge for a no-PR branch that already merged the target or whose rebase conflicts.

process_issues.description: Not spawned: review-context (no spec/protocol/infra surface), review-workflow-safety (no workflow change), review-spec (no closing reference or spec source), review-maintainability (off the default roster). Dropped below the finding bar: a conventions nit on ADR line wrap that cites no written rule, a simplicity nit on the `rebaseConflicted` flag whose only cost was diagnostic, and a docs re-raise of the already-posted mergeTargetInto JSDoc nit.
Read only the first 110 lines of merge-gate-fresh-base.test.ts, so the later test helpers (conflictingRebase, isRebase/isAbort, failGit) were not checked for simplicity.
Did not read decision 146 or find any ADR-numbering guard, so 0190's numbering gap (no 0188/0189 in tree) was not checked against that decision.
